What is Firebase: Firebase is a comprehensive app development platform by Google. Provides backend services: authentication, real-time database, Firestore, storage, hosting, functions, analytics, and more. Serverless — no infrastructure management. Acquired by Google in 2014.

# Firebase services overview
# Firestore: NoSQL document database
# Auth: user authentication
# Storage: file uploads
# Hosting: web hosting
# Functions: serverless backend
# Analytics: app tracking
# Messaging: push notifications
Firebase Console & Setup: Start at console.firebase.google.com. Create a project, register your app (iOS/Android/Web), and add the Firebase SDK. Firebase CLI for local development: emulators, deployment, and cloud functions.

# Install Firebase CLI
npm install -g firebase-tools

# Login
firebase login

# Init a project
firebase init
# Select: Firestore, Functions, Hosting, etc.

# Start emulators (local dev)
firebase emulators:start

# Deploy to production
firebase deploy
Firebase vs Firestore: Firebase has two database options: Realtime Database (JSON tree, real-time sync, low latency) and Firestore (document/collection model, richer queries, multi-region, better scaling). Firestore is recommended for new projects.
Firebase SDKs: Multiple SDKs: Web (JS/TS), iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin/Java), Flutter, Unity, C++, Admin SDK (server-side, Node.js/Python/Go/Java). The Web SDK comes in modular (v9+) and namespaced (v8) flavors.
Firebase Emulators: Local emulators for Firestore, Auth, Functions, Storage, Hosting, and PubSub. Enables offline development without touching production. Data persisted between sessions or cleared on restart.

Email & Password Auth: Built-in email/password authentication. createUserWithEmailAndPassword() for signup, signInWithEmailAndPassword() for login. Additional: email verification, password reset, profile management.
Google Sign-In: One-tap Google sign-in using Firebase Auth + Google provider. Configure OAuth consent screen and enable Google in Firebase Console Auth -> Sign-in method.
Anonymous Auth: Create temporary anonymous accounts. Convert to permanent by linking credentials. Useful for cart/activity before user signs up. signInAnonymously() creates a transient user.
Security Rules (Auth): Firestore Security Rules control who can read/write data. Built on Firebase Auth UID. Regular + recursive wildcards. Rules are evaluated on every request — keep them strict.

Documents & Collections: Firestore is a NoSQL document database. Data organized as documents (in collections). Documents contain key-value pairs. Subcollections for nested data. Documents have a max size of 1 MiB.
CRUD Operations: addDoc creates auto-ID. setDoc sets with known ID (or merges with merge:true). updateDoc updates specific fields. deleteDoc removes doc. Firestore does not support server-side UPDATE or DELETE with filters.
Queries & Filters: Firestore supports compound queries with where(), orderBy(), limit(), startAt/startAfter/endAt/endBefore. Composite indexes required for certain queries. No 'OR' queries — use multiple queries or in() for up to 10 values.
Real-time Listeners: onSnapshot() registers a real-time listener. Fires immediately with current data and again on every change. Returns an unsubscribe function. Use with a cleanup in component lifecycle.
Batched Writes & Transactions: batchedWrite executes multiple writes atomically (up to 500). runTransaction performs a read-then-write with automatic retry. Use transactions for counters, balances, and reservations.

Cloud Storage: Firebase Storage for user-generated content (images, videos, files). Uses GCS underneath. Security Rules based on auth. Upload with put() / putString(), download with getDownloadURL().
Firebase Hosting: Host web apps, microservices, or static content. Supports custom domains, SSL, CDN (via Fastly). Deploy with firebase deploy --only hosting. Dynamic content via Cloud Functions or Cloud Run rewrites.
Storage Security Rules: Storage Security Rules control file access. Validate file size, content type, and auth status. Path pattern matching with {wildcards}.

HTTP Functions: Cloud Functions runs serverless backend code (Node.js, Python, Go, Java, PHP, Ruby, .NET). Triggers: HTTP, Firestore changes, Auth events, Storage events, PubSub, Scheduled. Request/response with Express-like API.
Firestore Triggers: Trigger functions on Firestore document events: onCreate, onUpdate, onDelete, onWrite. Access to snap (new) and context (event info). Useful for denormalization, notifications, aggregation.
Auth & Scheduled Triggers: Auth triggers on user creation/deletion. Scheduled functions with cron syntax. Use for cleanup, reports, data sync. Functions time out at 60s (HTTP) or 540s (background).
Admin SDK: Firebase Admin SDK runs in privileged environments (server, Cloud Functions). Can bypass security rules. Supports: Firestore, Auth, Storage, FCM (messaging), Machine Learning. Initialize with service account JSON.

Firestore Data Modeling: NoSQL design for Firestore: denormalize, avoid joins, use subcollections for hierarchical data. Patterns: root collections for top-level entities, subcollections for related data, references for many-to-many.
Security Rules Deep: Security rules can validate data on write (request.resource), check existing data (resource), enforce types, sizes, and complex conditions. Rules are evaluated every request — test thoroughly.
Performance & Costs: Firestore costs: reads, writes, deletes, and stored data. Avoid unindexed queries (full scan). Use collection group indexes for subcollection queries. Limit with listener count. Use offline persistence.
Firebase Cloud Messaging: FCM sends push notifications and data messages to client apps. Topics for pub/sub (any client subscribed can receive). Device groups for multi-device. Admin SDK for server-side sending.
Analytics & Crashlytics: Firebase Analytics tracks user events automatically (screen views, user properties) and custom events. Crashlytics reports app crashes with stack traces, logs, and non-fatal errors.

Security Rules Deep Dive: Firebase Security Rules protect Firestore, Storage, and RTDB. Rules are evaluated on every request using a declarative syntax. Key patterns: request.auth for auth checks, resource.data for existing data, request.resource.data for incoming writes. Use granular rules: match /users/{userId} { allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId; }. Validate data: request.resource.data.keys().hasAll(['name', 'email']). Firestore security rules can check for data types (value is number), limits (value >= 0), and string patterns.
Firebase Extensions & Cloud Functions: Firebase Extensions are pre-built solutions for common tasks (resize images, send emails, translate text). Cloud Functions (v2) use Cloud Run with Eventarc triggers. Functions can respond to Firestore changes, auth events, storage uploads, and scheduled tasks. onDocumentCreated, onDocumentUpdated, onRequest, onSchedule. Use environment variables for config (functions.config()). Cold starts are mitigated by minimum instances. Function memory/timeout: 256MB/30s default, up to 16GB/540s. Region selection affects latency.
